paragraphs: There was once a Hindu queen whose deepest wish was that every one of her children would reach spiritual freedom in this very life. So she didn't hand them over to nurses; she looked after them herself. Every night, as she rocked them to sleep, she sang them the same single song: 'Tat tvam asi' — 'That thou art.'
Three of her children grew up to become sannyasins, monks who gave up the world. The fourth child, though, was taken away to be raised elsewhere so that he could one day become king.
As he was leaving home, his mother pressed a folded piece of paper into his hand and told him to read it only when he had grown into a man.

Years later the prince unfolded it. It said that God alone is true and everything else is false; that the soul never kills and is never killed; and that he should live alone or in the company of holy people. The moment he read it, the young prince too renounced the world and became a sannyasin.
learn: What we hear over and over in childhood quietly shapes who we become. Choose carefully what you repeat to yourself every day. One clear truth, held onto, can redirect an entire life.
